newsitem.title: USA: SBC asks U.S. court to overturn FCC order.
newsitem.headline: SBC asks U.S. court to overturn FCC order.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc said Thursday it asked a U.S. court to overturn new federal rules setting aside $2.25 billion a year to wire schools and libraries to the Internet.
The Federal Communications Commission rules are a part of the agency's overhaul last month of the $23 billion web of telephone company subsidies.
SBC also expects to ask the U.S. appeals court in St. Louis to suspend key parts of the FCC's "universal service" rules while the judges consider the carrier's request.

"While we strongly support the provision of telecommunications technology to schools throughout the country, SBC opposes the FCC's proposal of a new tax, hidden in the telephone bills of each of our customers, to provide goods and services that were not contemplated by the (1996 telecommunications) law," SBC Senior Vice President Zeke Robertson said in a statement.
Robertson said the program was "not contemplated by Congress or authorized by the (telecom) act."
Robertson added that SBC has long supported improving education throughout the seven states it serves.
Earlier this week SBC asked the St. Louis-based court to overturn the FCC rules that overhaul phone charges and are designed to reduce monthly phone bills.
